thread:
Ana: Heads-up — Caravel QBR next Wed 10am PT. Need final token-burn forecast + any anomalies we should call out to execs. Two asks: 1) FinOps numbers for 90d run-rate and projected 30/60/90 day burn, 2) Ops/Enablement recommendations to reduce embed token usage before renewal. Also flagging potential renewal risk: customer mentioned a near-term budget freeze in yesterday's call.
Sam: On it. I'll pull the 90d run-rate and a quick variance breakdown by route. Initial glance: weekly batch webhook spikes account for ~28% of token volume. Might be an easy throttle.
Lee: I can lead an enablement drop-in for their infra/product next Tue. Proposed agenda: batching patterns, cache TTLs, and light-weight quantization guidance for their offline workers. 30-45m. Is that ok?
Jon: For the spike - do they use streaming responses or full payloads? If full, switching to chunked streaming and shorter max_tokens per call helps. Also suggest prefix KV caching for common prompts. Example config we recommend: ```json
{"cache": {"enabled": true, "prefix_ttl_s": 86400}, "batching": {"max_batch_size": 16, "latency_slo_ms": 200}}
```
Nadia: FYI sales flagged a budget freeze, so renewal risk = medium-high unless we show quick cost mitigation. I can offer a short-term 3-mo commit with a 10% discount as a bridge. Need cost delta numbers to propose.
Sam: SQL I ran to get per-route token burn for last 90d: ```sql
SELECT route, SUM(tokens) as tokens_sum, COUNT(*) as calls
FROM api_calls
WHERE customer_id = 'caravel' AND ts >= now() - interval '90 days'
GROUP BY route
ORDER BY tokens_sum DESC
LIMIT 20;
```
Will paste results in a follow-up message in 30m.
Ana: Great. Can someone sketch recommended budget-alert thresholds we can push to their billing/admins? They want low-noise but early warnings.
Jon: Suggest thresholds: 60% (info), 85% (action), 100% (block/notify). Minimal payload for their alerting webhook: ```json
{"thresholds": [{"pct": 60, "notify": ["ops@caravel.com"]}, {"pct": 85, "notify": ["owner@caravel.com","cs@redwood.com"]}, {"pct": 100, "notify": ["finance@redwood.com"], "auto_block": false} ]}
```
Sam: I'll generate a 30/60/90 projection table and include the impact of a 3-mo commit + 10% discount. Quick note: if they enable prefix caching + throttle batch job from hourly->daily at night, estimated token reduction = ~22% (conservative).
Lee: I'll make a 1-pager play for the enablement session (slides + 2 sample code snippets for prefix caching + example request batching). Want to sync with Jon to make sure the code matches runtime caveats.
Nadia: I'll draft the renewal note to legal/sales with the proposed bridge commit. If FinOps + Enablement can confirm savings within 48h, I can push the offer.
deploy-bot: Budget alert created: Caravel monthly threshold set at $12,000. Current month utilization = $14,400 (120%). Triggering: #billing-alerts.
Ana: Thanks — that alert explains exec concern. Action items: Sam -> deliver 90d run-rate + 30/60/90 projections (due EOD today). Jon + Lee -> enablement playbook + config snippets (due tomorrow). Nadia -> prepare bridge offer draft (needs numbers). I'll own QBR deck sections for "Cost & Risk" and "Enablement plan".
Sam: Pulling numbers now, will post CSV.
Jon: I'll pair with Lee tomorrow morning to finalize snippets.
Lee: Added tentative enablement meeting invite for Tue 11am PT and included caravel eng and product.
Ana: Perfect — if we can show a clear >15% near-term reduction and the bridge commit, renewal conversation should go neutral->positive. I'll update the QBR template once Sam posts the projections. :thumbsup:
